questions.demand: Velocity direction from x(t) and y(t).
questions.source_custody_status: SOURCE_CUSTODY_HOLD: competitive-bank verified demand is not ordinary Core2 custody; bank record is adapted/CANDIDATE.
questions.learner_eligibility_basis: Question-set selector has not established learner eligibility.

analysis.B_real_bottleneck: Recognize that instantaneous velocity direction comes from velocity components, not the position vector; the source route additionally requires differentiation.
analysis.C_prerequisite_assumed: Differentiation of x(t), y(t) to obtain v_x, v_y; not established in this canonical bucket.
analysis.D_canonical_teaching: Canonical teaching is Split one plane-motion event into independent x/y components with one clock: Perpendicular components may be solved separately because each axis equation contains only that axis's quantities, but they still describe one object at one physical time.
analysis.E_extension_or_bridge: The canonical bucket explicitly excludes calculus-based differentiation of a time-dependent position vector. After velocity components are known, simultaneous-component reconstruction is canonical; obtaining them by differentiation is not.
analysis.J_hold_or_gap: The canonical bucket explicitly excludes calculus-based differentiation of a time-dependent position vector. After velocity components are known, simultaneous-component reconstruction is canonical; obtaining them by differentiation is not.

questions.source_custody_status: SOURCE_CUSTODY_HOLD: competitive-bank verified demand is not ordinary Core2 custody; bank record is adapted/CANDIDATE.
questions.learner_eligibility_basis: Owner learner-set policy excludes JEE Advanced; retained as diagnostic demand evidence.

analysis.B_real_bottleneck: Translate the collision/energy change into the post-bounce vertical state before applying projectile height reasoning.
analysis.C_prerequisite_assumed: Energy/restitution treatment across an impact; not established by this package.
analysis.D_canonical_teaching: Canonical teaching is Select the gravity-only projectile model before using projectile consequences: After release in the ideal near-Earth model, projectile motion is not a new set of laws: it is the same component kinematics with a_x=0 and a_y=-g (for +y upward).
analysis.E_extension_or_bridge: Both candidate records exercise projectile consequences but also require energy/restitution machinery outside the bounded Motion-in-2D package. Owner-label identity remains unresolved.
analysis.J_hold_or_gap: QUESTION_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS plus learner exclusion and extension boundary

analysis.B_real_bottleneck: Reject constant-acceleration projectile equations and solve the velocity-dependent horizontal model.
analysis.C_prerequisite_assumed: Newton-II differential equation and exponential/integral solution for linear drag; not established here.
analysis.D_canonical_teaching: Canonical teaching is Apply constant-acceleration kinematics component by component: The one-dimensional constant-acceleration equations can be applied to each perpendicular component independently when a_x and a_y are each constant over the same interval.
analysis.E_extension_or_bridge: Linear drag makes acceleration velocity-dependent. The canonical bucket explicitly excludes drag and licenses constant-acceleration equations only when each component acceleration is constant.
